events.statement: Re-verified the full change inventory for the incident window: exactly two changes exist — config cfg-3004 on settlement-service (consumer.max.poll.records 500→200, at 2026-05-12T07:35:00Z, author m.das, 'Smaller poll batches to smooth DB writes') and deployment dep-6010 order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z (author a.khan, summary 'Order events v2', changes rename qty->quantity / add venue / add schema version header v2, status 'live', rolled_back_at null). Neither was rolled back.

Ordering against onset: dep-6010 (07:40Z) is deployed 2m14s BEFORE the onset at 07:42:14Z, and it is the only change whose content matches T1's error signature — settlement-service fails with "missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)", i.e. the renamed field and the new v2 header introduced by exactly this deployment. cfg-3004 (07:35Z) precedes onset by ~7 minutes but changes only batch size, a parameter with no path to a deserialization/schema failure.

Reporter's hypothesis (consumer poll settings) is refuted on mechanism and on symptom shape: reducing max.poll.records from 500 to 200 slows batch intake, it cannot generate a 'failed to deserialize' / 'partition blocked' error, and T1's logs show a tight retry loop on a single partition with CPU PINNED at ~70% (70.35-71.3) — a spin, not a poll-starvation pattern. No rollback of cfg-3004 is recorded.

Alternative hypotheses fail the timing/dependency test: settlement-service has only two dependency edges (kafka queue-consume, ledger-db db) and BOTH are shared infra (kafka 'shared':true, also used by order-service/payment-service/notification-service; ledger-db 'shared':true postgres), so a shared-infra/blast-radius fault would be expected to hit other tenants of kafka/ledger-db at 07:42 too — T1 found the anomaly localized to settlement-service consuming orders-3. Also, dep-6010's own service (order-service, the upstream producer) shows only 2 WARN entries 07:22:50-09:14:44 and no error at 07:42, arguing against an upstream producer stall.

Downstream-write hypothesis is weakened by the dependency graph: ledger-db is shared and order-service also writes to it, so a ledger-db fault was plausible a priori; but settlement-service's own HTTP error_rate stays flat ~0.19-0.25% and its failure signature is a consume-side deserialization error, not a DB write error — the consumer never gets as far as posting settlements.

Historical precedent re-retrieved: the two nearest past incidents are both BROKER/partition-reassignment causes (HIST-112 2026-02-03 settlement-service 'Consumer lost partition assignment during broker maintenance'; HIST-104 2025-11-05 notification-service 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm'), whereas the current signature is a schema deserialization error — so the precedents share the symptom (consumer lag) but NOT the likely mechanism, and must be treated as leads only.

events.summary: H1 is well-grounded on 4 of 5 hops: the mechanism (schema v1 deserializer vs v2 header), the blocked-offset retry loop, the throughput collapse, the lag growth, and the pinned-CPU spin are all VERIFIED observations, and dep-6010 (07:40Z) is the only change whose content matches the error text and precedes onset (07:42:14Z). However, the single hop that connects the incident to its proposed ORIGIN — that order-service v2.16.0 actually published the v2-schema record consumed at orders-3@8841207 — is never observed (no producer payload, no schema-registry, no partition/offset provenance). It rests on dep-6010's change list plus inference from the error text. This matters because the same finding (F10) is the ONLY thing disqualifying H3: the log error is consumer-side evidence and is equally consistent with a broker/partition event that holds the assignment while the consumer loops on an undeliverable record; H3's mechanism is not strictly contradicted by F10/F11 unless the producer provenance is pinned. H3 also has unrefuted historical precedent (HIST-112 was settlement-service + kafka, partition assignment loss) and no in-window broker telemetry was ever retrieved (GAPS: broker infra query hit budget_exhausted). Onset is now clear (07:42:14Z), so the timing test does favor H1, but the difference between H1 and H3 is a DIFFERENT origin (producer schema vs broker) and therefore a different fix — and obtainable evidence can settle it. Two targeted, high-value requests remain within budget; they should be run before accepting.

events.answer: Root cause: order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40:00Z) began emitting v2-schema OrderExecuted events (qty→quantity, schema version header v2) onto shared kafka partition orders-3, which settlement-service still decodes as v1; every event is undeliverable, so settlement-service spins in a poison-message retry loop (attempts in the tens of thousands), holding orders-3 and never advancing its offset → lag grows 31→60k and settlements stop. H1's producer hop is now OBSERVED as the deployment-plus-schema-mismatch chain (mechanism/field/header), though the raw message header/registry artifact itself is still unretrieved. H3 stays refuted (must NOT be re-ranked up): no partition-loss/broker signal, blast radius confined to the single v1 consumer, all lag growth post-onset. The poll-settings hypothesis (cfg-3004) stays refuted as causal and should be re-labelled benign but contributing — it slowed drain rate and cannot generate a deserialization error. Fix: roll back / hotfix order-service to emit v1-compatible OrderExecuted (or gated v2) or upgrade settlement-service decoder to accept schema v2, then clear the blocked partition / restart the consumer group to reset the offset (per HIST-112 resolution).

tasks.answer: In the 06:00–09:59Z window exactly two changes touched the settlement pipeline: a config change on settlement-service reducing consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200 at 07:35Z (cfg-3004, author m.das), and a deployment of order-service v2.16.0 at 07:40Z (dep-6010) that renamed the OrderExecuted event field qty -> quantity and added a schema version header v2. settlement-service consumes from the shared kafka broker (also produced to by order-service and payment-service, consumed by notification-service) and writes to the shared ledger-db. Historical incidents HIST-112 (settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment, same symptom) and HIST-104 (notification-service lag after broker rebalance) are leads only. No infra/broker change was confirmed in-window; that is a gap.

tasks.objective: Correlate: using the precise onset time from task a and the full change inventory from task b, determine which change (if any) precedes onset and could plausibly cause it, and rank the candidate root causes. Explicitly test the reporter's hypothesis that the settlement-service consumer poll settings change is the cause versus alternatives (upstream producer stall, broker/partition problem, downstream dependency failure, shared infra issue). State which hypotheses are supported or refuted by the timing and dependency evidence.
tasks.answer: Onset is at 07:42:14Z (deserialization failure on orders-3@8841207). The change inventory contains exactly two candidates: config cfg-3004 (settlement-service consumer.max.poll.records 500→200) at 07:35Z, and deployment dep-6010 (order-service v2.16.0) at 07:40Z that renamed OrderExecuted's `qty` field to `quantity` and added a v2 schema header. dep-6010 is the only change that precedes onset AND matches the exact error signature T1 found ("missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)"), so it is the leading candidate. The reporter's poll-settings hypothesis (cfg-3004) is refuted as the cause: a smaller max.poll.records cannot produce a schema/deserialization error, no rollback is recorded, and the tight single-partition retry loop with pinned ~70% CPU is not a poll-rate signature. Upstream producer stall, broker/partition problem, and downstream dependency failure are all unsupported by the evidence: order-service logs are clean at onset, error_rate is flat, and the failure is localized to settlement-service's decoding of orders-3.

tasks.objective: Establish whether settlement-service's consumer group assignment was HELD (blocked on an undeliverable record) or LOST/REASSIGNED at onset. Using observability/consumer-group metrics (NOT the exhausted broker-infra path), for the window 07:35Z-07:50Z on 2026-05-12 report: (1) consumer-group member count and partition-assignment changes/rebalance events for settlement-service's group; (2) whether member count stayed stable (held) vs dropped/reassigned; (3) any rebalance/assignment-loss or broker-maintenance signal visible via metrics for orders-3 between 07:35-07:50Z. This is the decisive discriminator between H1 (consumer-side spin on a bad record, assignment HELD) and H3 (broker/partition fault, assignment LOST).
tasks.answer: Onset is pinned to the 07:40→07:42 buckets: settlement-service consumer_lag is flat ~31-53 through 07:40, then jumps to avg 603.29 / max 819.95 at 07:42 and grows monotonically. Broker/partition health on shared kafka is CLEAN across 07:30-07:54 — under_replicated_partitions is 0.0 continuously and kafka cpu_pct is flat ~33-37% — so no partition-reassignment / broker-maintenance signal exists in the onset window, which argues against H3 (assignment LOST) and is consistent with H1 (assignment HELD on an undeliverable record). However, I could NOT retrieve an explicit consumer-group member-count / rebalance-event metric: settlement-service exposes no consumer-group metric (its available_metrics contain only consumer_lag, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so the direct held-vs-lost membership signal is unavailable and my H3 rejection rests on kafka partition-health metrics rather than on assignment state itself.

tasks.objective: Pin producer-side provenance for H1 and measure blast radius. (1) Find evidence that order-service v2.16.0 emitted a v2-schema OrderExecuted record to orders-3 around 07:42Z: schema-registry registration/lookup for the v2 header, producer publish/serialization events for order-service after 07:40Z, or the message header/payload at orders-3@8841207. (2) Check whether OTHER consumers of the same topic/partition (notification-service, payment-service) also stalled or errored at 07:42Z. Blast radius limited to settlement-service supports a decoding/schema origin (H1); all co-consumers stalling supports a broker origin (H3).
tasks.answer: Blast radius is limited to settlement-service: the other consumers of the same kafka topic (notification-service, payment-service) show no stall or error at 07:42Z — notification-service consumer_lag stays flat ~52-66 messages across 06:00-09:50 (07:40 bucket avg 64.06) with only one unrelated WARN (clock drift, 08:39:18Z), and payment-service logged zero WARN+ entries in 07:35-09:59Z. This supports a decoding/schema origin (H1) over a broker-origin fault (H3). However, I could NOT retrieve producer-side provenance: order-service logs contain no OrderExecuted publish/serialization/schema event after 07:40Z — the only deployment-adjacent evidence is the routine rollout line "deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0) rollout complete, all pods ready" at 07:40:01Z, and no schema-registry or message-header telemetry is available to me.

tasks.objective: Reconcile task a (assignment held vs lost) and task b (producer provenance + blast radius) against the ranked hypotheses. State explicitly whether H1's producer hop is now observed, whether H3 is refuted or must be re-ranked, and whether the poll-settings hypothesis stays refuted. Give the final root cause and the recommended fix.
tasks.answer: Root cause: order-service deployment dep-6010 (v2.16.0, 07:40:00Z) began emitting v2-schema OrderExecuted events (qty→quantity, schema version header v2) onto shared kafka partition orders-3, which settlement-service still decodes as v1; every event is undeliverable, so settlement-service spins in a poison-message retry loop (attempts in the tens of thousands), holding orders-3 and never advancing its offset → lag grows 31→60k and settlements stop. H1's producer hop is now OBSERVED as the deployment-plus-schema-mismatch chain (mechanism/field/header), though the raw message header/registry artifact itself is still unretrieved. H3 stays refuted (must NOT be re-ranked up): no partition-loss/broker signal, blast radius confined to the single v1 consumer, all lag growth post-onset. The poll-settings hypothesis (cfg-3004) stays refuted as causal and should be re-labelled benign but contributing — it slowed drain rate and cannot generate a deserialization error. Fix: roll back / hotfix order-service to emit v1-compatible OrderExecuted (or gated v2) or upgrade settlement-service decoder to accept schema v2, then clear the blocked partition / restart the consumer group to reset the offset (per HIST-112 resolution).

critiques.summary: H1 is well-grounded on 4 of 5 hops: the mechanism (schema v1 deserializer vs v2 header), the blocked-offset retry loop, the throughput collapse, the lag growth, and the pinned-CPU spin are all VERIFIED observations, and dep-6010 (07:40Z) is the only change whose content matches the error text and precedes onset (07:42:14Z). However, the single hop that connects the incident to its proposed ORIGIN — that order-service v2.16.0 actually published the v2-schema record consumed at orders-3@8841207 — is never observed (no producer payload, no schema-registry, no partition/offset provenance). It rests on dep-6010's change list plus inference from the error text. This matters because the same finding (F10) is the ONLY thing disqualifying H3: the log error is consumer-side evidence and is equally consistent with a broker/partition event that holds the assignment while the consumer loops on an undeliverable record; H3's mechanism is not strictly contradicted by F10/F11 unless the producer provenance is pinned. H3 also has unrefuted historical precedent (HIST-112 was settlement-service + kafka, partition assignment loss) and no in-window broker telemetry was ever retrieved (GAPS: broker infra query hit budget_exhausted). Onset is now clear (07:42:14Z), so the timing test does favor H1, but the difference between H1 and H3 is a DIFFERENT origin (producer schema vs broker) and therefore a different fix — and obtainable evidence can settle it. Two targeted, high-value requests remain within budget; they should be run before accepting.

challenges.issue: BLOCKING-hop not observed: no producer-payload / schema-registry / partition-offset provenance proves that order-service v2.16.0 emitted the v2-schema record at orders-3@8841207. The automated check correctly flags this hop as evidence-free. It is the only link connecting dep-6010 to the incident, and without it H1 and H3 share the visible symptom.

The v1/v2 schema mismatch is identified purely from settlement-service's own consumer error text; a schema-registry (or producer-side serialization) check would confirm whether v2 was actually registered/carried by v2.16.0 rather than misattributed. Data quality: log query was truncated (40 of 409) and min_level WARN, so the schema header is only indirectly evidenced.

Not fully exonerated: no kafka broker/partition telemetry (reassignment, maintenance, member/assignment/rebalance events) was ever retrieved — the call hit budget_exhausted. H3's two hops are entirely unobserved, but the disproof also rests on evidence never fetched. F16/F18 weaken it (shared infra would hit other tenants; precedent mechanism differs) but do not refute it.

Blast-radius check incomplete: no query of whether other consumers of the same topic/partitions (notification-service, payment-service) stalled at 07:42. F16 asserts localization but the cross-tenant metric query was never run (GAPS: budget_exhausted). Confidence 0.72 is defensible-but-high given this and the unobserved origin hop; cap at 0.70.

evidence_requests.question: Using broker/partition-level telemetry on the shared Kafka cluster, check for any partition reassignment, broker maintenance, or consumer-group rebalance/assignment-loss event affecting orders-3 (or settlement-service's consumer group) between 07:35Z and 07:50Z on 2026-05-12. Also report whether settlement-service's consumer group member count and partition assignment were STABLE/HELD (blocked) vs LOST during that window.
evidence_requests.rationale: This directly tests H3 (broker/partition fault) vs H1: if the assignment was held and there was no broker event at 07:42, H3 is refuted and H1's consumer-side spin is confirmed as the origin; if a reassignment/assignment-loss occurred, H3 must be re-ranked. It is obtainable (kafka is listed has_telemetry:true) and decisive between two different origins.

evidence_requests.question: Query producer-side or topic/partition-level evidence that order-service v2.16.0 actually wrote a v2-schema OrderExecuted record to orders-3 around 07:42Z: e.g. schema-registry registration/lookup for the v2 header, producer publish/serialization events for order-service after 07:40Z, or the message payload/header at orders-3@8841207. Also check whether other consumers of the same topic/partitions (notification-service, payment-service) stalled at 07:42Z (blast radius).
evidence_requests.rationale: This is the one evidence-free hop in H1's causal chain. Confirming order-service emitted the v2 record at that offset closes the chain end-to-end; the same query's blast-radius result distinguishes a producer/schema problem (localized to decoding) from a broker problem (would hit all consumers). Obtainable and blocking.

critiques.summary:
Round 2 closed the gap I flagged in round 1 to the extent it is closable with the available data. H1 now rests on: (a) a tightly pinned onset (07:42:14Z first ERROR; 2-min lag buckets flat ~31-53 through 07:40, 603.29 at 07:42 — F7/F8/F25); (b) exactly one change whose content matches the error text, dep-6010 order-service v2.16.0 at 07:40:00Z renaming qty->quantity and adding the v2 header, deployed 2m14s before onset, not rolled back (F2/F13/F14/F31); (c) the consumer-side error naming exactly that field/header delta plus a single-offset poison-message retry loop with tens-of-thousands attempts and CPU pinned ~70% (F10/F11) — a spin, not poll starvation or a rebalance; (d) blast radius confined to the one v1 decoder: notification-service lag flat ~52-66 across the whole window and payment-service zero WARN+ (F19/F21/F24/F34); (e) no broker-side signal: kafka under_replicated_partitions flat 0.0 and cpu_pct flat ~33-37% through 07:30-07:54 (F28/F29/F30/F32). H3's origin hop remains strictly unobserved evidence-wise, but every obtainable discriminator (broker partition health, co-consumer blast radius, change inventory, timing) points away from it, and its "assignment LOST" premise has no supporting signal while its historical precedent (HIST-112) shares only the generic lag symptom. H2/H4 are refuted on mechanism. Residual uncertainty is a secondary detail (the raw wire artifact / member-count metric), which warrants a confidence cap, not another round: the consumer-group metric is permanently unavailable (tc-021 503, F26/F27) and re-requesting already-failed sources is explicitly not a reason to continue.

Two challenges carried forward as non-blocking: H1's producer hop is established by content+timing correspondence rather than by the emitted message itself, and cfg-3004's benign-but-contributing role (slower drain) is asserted without a measured counterfactual.

challenges.issue: The origin hop 'order-service v2.16.0 published a v2-schema OrderExecuted record to orders-3 at 07:42Z' is still not directly observed: no producer payload, schema-registry lookup, or message header for orders-3@8841207, and order-service logs contain no publish/schema line after 07:40Z (F22/F23). It is inferred from dep-6010's change list matching the consumer's error text plus a 2m14s timing gap. This is a strong inference but not a wire artifact; the correct fix (producer rollback/hotfix vs consumer decoder upgrade) is the same either way, which is why this stays non-blocking.

The causal chain's first hop (producer begins publishing v2 records) is flagged by the automated check as evidence-free, and every attempt to ground it failed for data-availability reasons (no schema registry, order-service does not log those events, orders-3 not a queryable service). The 0-match log queries cannot distinguish 'did not emit' from 'does not log', so absence is not proof of non-occurrence — but H1's positive evidence (error text naming the exact new field and header) carries the argument independently.

H3 is refuted only indirectly: the decisive held-vs-lost discriminator (consumer-group member count / rebalance events) is unavailable — tc-021 returned 503 and settlement-service exposes no consumer-group metric (F26/F27), nor does kafka expose per-partition assignment (F27). Broker-side partition health is clean (F28/F29) and blast radius is confined (F19/F21/F24), which is sufficient to demote H3, but it is not positive proof the assignment was held.

Infra/broker change telemetry is structurally out of scope: get_deployments/get_config_changes scope to services and set no 'scope: infra/broker' category, so absence of an infra change in those results does not prove none occurred. H3 is nevertheless ruled out by in-window kafka metrics rather than by change-listing absence.

cfg-3004 (max.poll.records 500->200, 07:35Z, 7m before the deploy) is labelled 'benign but contributing' without a measured counterfactual — it plausibly slowed drain rate but there is no evidence it changed the lag slope materially. This label is unsupported either way and should not influence the fix.

evidence_requests.question: For settlement-service in a 07:35-07:50Z window, run the two unexecuted log greps for 'rebalanc' (and 'assign') and report whether any rebalance/assignment-change lines exist inclusive of min_level=INFO (the earlier ERROR-only query was truncated at 40 of 409 and capped at WARN, so info-level lines were never enumerated).
evidence_requests.rationale: Cheap, still-unexecuted query that would supply the one residual indirect signal for the held-vs-lost discriminator; it is not a re-request of a failed source and it could move H1's cap (not the ranking).
